column1: # Canonical DistSQL query dispatch and response-consumption runtime ownership.

column5: An already-built immutable TransportRequest crosses a caller-injected QueryTransport and yields one pull-based raw QueryResponse owner rather than a pre-decoded iterator. QueryResultContext carries the final field layout and shared warning handler through both Select entry points without parallel argument drift; QuerySelectResult retains that state plus close ownership, Select and SelectWithRuntimeStats transfer the response exactly once into the existing lazy decoder, and Analyze and Checksum preserve ordered next_raw bytes without protobuf decoding. Result labels, store, paging, concurrency, plan IDs, restricted SQL type, ANALYZE request source, nil-response failure, first transport error, raw source error, and close ownership are structural. Concrete TiKV/TiFlash routing, protobuf RPC construction, retries, cancellation, caching, memory accounting, response-close error propagation, a non-nil subset returned together with an error, asynchronous production, and full runtime-stat formatting remain external.

QuerySelectResult is the raw response and lifecycle owner: a raw pull removes exactly that subset, and consuming Select conversion transfers the remaining owner and feeds each remaining QueryResultSubset's data plus same-pull runtime metadata into the existing SelectResponseIter once. The decoder validates response errors and intermediate layout, preserves coded TiKV warnings, lazily decodes final then reverse-priority intermediate channels, materializes source-proven TypeDefault and TypeChunk scalar rows, and merges runtime data only from the subset that carried it. ResponseChannel is only a deterministic QueryResponse adapter; open pending, first source error, order, natural exhaustion, and idempotent explicit close stay distinct. Concrete blocking TiKV transport, response-close errors, simultaneous subset-plus-error stats, temporal/timezone Datum materialization, CHBlock, full cop runtime detail/telemetry, memory accounting, a production table reader, and sorted heap merging remain open.
